chapters.title: Three appraisals, three different questions
chapters.lede: Eduversal runs three appraisal systems. Each one looks at something different, uses its own evidence and gives its own result. Knowing which one you are in is the first step.

blocks.lead: Appraisal is how your school, your teachers and you as a leader learn **what is working and what should improve** — with evidence, fairly, and once a year.
points: **Teacher Appraisal** looks at one teacher's professional practice. Your school's own appraisers run it.
**School Appraisal** looks at the whole school across five domains, through a year-round visit cycle with Eduversal.
**Principal Appraisal** looks at the Principal's leadership. The school team does not score the Principal.
The three are **never merged** into one score or one rubric.
check: Never merge Teacher Appraisal, School Appraisal, and Principal Appraisal into one score or one rubric

items.title: Teacher Appraisal
facts: Your school's own appraisers — Subject Leader / Head of Department, Principal, Academic or Cambridge Coordinator
At least 3 formal lesson observations per semester, recorded in Edunav
A score out of 100 and a grade A–F, once a year

items.title: School Appraisal
facts: Eduversal Domain Leads, using your school's evidence
Self-Evaluation, two on-site visits, the Evidence Guide workbook
A Development Rating for each of the five domains — no overall school score

items.title: Principal Appraisal
facts: The Chief Academic Officer (CAO) or a designated Eduversal Academic Director
Operating cadence, two leadership observations, 360 feedback, outcomes, self-reflection
A score, an A–F band and a recommendation

blocks.title: Who is not appraised yet
blocks.text: Teachers who are still in induction **stay in Teacher Induction** and do not enter Teacher Appraisal until induction is formally completed. **Year-1 Principals** follow the Principal Induction and are not formally appraised.

source.at: School Admin Team — What You Actually Use

check: do not enter Teacher Appraisal until induction is formally completed

chapters.title: How a teacher's year is appraised
chapters.lede: Your school owns the teacher's score. Eduversal visits help teachers grow, but they never change a score.

items.label: Principal walkthrough

blocks.title: What makes up the final score
blocks.intro: Four frameworks are combined into one score out of 100. Early Years teachers do not have a Student Survey, so Class Observation carries more weight.

items.name: F2 · Class Observation
items.desc: The mean of all valid formal observations by your school's appraisers.

items.name: F1 · Teacher Administration
items.desc: Calendar, plans, lesson plans, records — collected by school management, checked by the appraiser.

items.name: F3 · Work Inspection
items.desc: Professional conduct and contribution, presented by the teacher at the End-of-Year Conference.

items.name: F4 · Student Survey
items.desc: End of each semester; the year's score is the mean of the two.

items.name: F2 · Class Observation
items.desc: Takes the 10% the Student Survey would carry.

items.name: F1 · Teacher Administration
items.desc: Early Years version of the framework.

items.name: F4 · Student Survey
items.desc: Not used — children in EY1–EY3 are too young to answer reliably.

source.at: §4 Summary Report; Early Years Composite Weighting

check: contributes 10% to the final appraisal composite

blocks.title: The teacher's year, step by step

steps.title: Orientation
steps.text: Eduversal briefs school management; each school then orients its own teachers.

steps.title: Formal observations
steps.text: At least 3 per semester. The appraiser reviews the lesson plan first — there is no face-to-face pre-conference.

steps.title: Glow · Grow · Go
steps.text: Right after each observation: one strength, one growth question, one agreed next step.

steps.title: End-of-Year Conference
steps.text: F3 is scored, F4 is calculated from both semesters, and the final score is worked out.

steps.title: Results & goals
steps.text: Scores are shared in Edunav and the teacher drafts a professional goal for next year.

blocks.title: Eduversal Specialist visits are formative
blocks.text: A Subject Specialist observes a lesson during each Eduversal visit and gives Glow / Grow / Go feedback **directly to the teacher**. This feedback **never enters** the F2 score, the final score or level progression. Only your school's formal observations count.

source.at: Who observes, and which observations count

check: It does not enter your F2 score, your composite, or your level progression

blocks.title: Choosing appraisers
blocks.text: An appraiser is a Subject Leader / Head of Department, the Principal, or the Academic or Cambridge Coordinator, holding a supervisor-level certification and at least three years of teaching experience. **A teacher's former induction mentor never appraises that teacher.**
check: at least three years of teaching experience
a mentor does not formally observe their own mentee

blocks.title: From score to grade
blocks.intro: Each framework's rubric average is turned into a score out of 100 (for example, an average of 3.0 = 75). The final score then gives the grade.

blocks.title: Moving up a level
blocks.intro: Meeting a threshold makes a teacher **eligible** — it does not guarantee a move. The appraiser recommends, school management confirms with Eduversal, and no move is possible in a year graded below B. A teacher who stays at the same level is in a developmental status, not a failure.

steps.title: Post-Induction → Developing
steps.text: F2 at least **65**, no F2 item below 2, F1 complete, and an Induction Completion Certificate marked “completed”.

steps.title: Developing → Proficient
steps.text: F2 at least **70**, at most two F2 items at 2 and none at 1, no active F3 concerns, one full year at Developing.

steps.title: Proficient → Lead
steps.text: F2 at least **78**, no F2 item below 3, F3 shows contribution beyond the classroom, written rationale from the appraiser.

chapters.title: Your school's year with Eduversal
chapters.lede: School Appraisal looks at the school as a whole. It runs as a cycle: Phases 0 to 3 in Semester I, and a short Impact Review near the end of the year.

items.label: domains
items.note: Leadership · Teaching & Learning · Curriculum · Student Outcomes · Culture & Community

items.label: on-site visits
items.note: Phase 1 and Phase 3, each with 5 Eduversal experts — one per domain.

items.label: working days before each visit
items.note: Your Self-Evaluation must be in. Without it, the visit is rescheduled.

items.label: after Phase 3
items.note: You receive the Annual School Quality Report — the only written report of the year.

check: a minimum of 5 working days before your visit date
within 3 weeks of your Phase 3 visit
Each on-site visit team has 5 experts

blocks.title: The cycle: Phase 0 to Phase 4
blocks.intro: Your school's exact dates and visiting team are shared separately in your school schedule. Phases 0–3 finish before teaching ends on 4 December 2026.

steps.name: Kickoff
steps.text: Introduces the cycle and launches your **Self-Evaluation**.

steps.name: Teaching Quality Visit
steps.text: Walkthroughs, Specialist lesson observations, interviews, domain meetings. Findings given **in person** at the oral exit report.

steps.name: Progress Check-in
steps.text: Progress review with your **Visit I Supervisor**.

steps.name: Validation Visit
steps.text: Validates your Self-Evaluation. Leads to the **Annual School Quality Report** and the two School Development Priorities.

steps.name: Impact Review
steps.text: Checks what changed for the two priorities. **Creates no new rating.**

blocks.title: The five domains
rows: Classroom practice and teaching quality — including your school's own F2 results, shown as a **school-level pattern**, never as individual scores
Assessment systems, student results, EASE Assessment data. EASE Growth Version 1 is **context only, not scored**.
School culture and climate, safeguarding, community engagement, staff well-being
check: EASE Growth Version 1 as context only (not scored)

blocks.title: Development Ratings — one for each domain
blocks.intro: Each domain gets its own rating, measured against the framework standard — **not against other schools**.

items.name: Needs Intervention
items.desc: Significant gaps. A mandatory action plan within 4 weeks, with targeted support.

items.name: Developing
items.desc: Good foundations; some systems need strengthening. Targeted support.

items.name: Strong
items.desc: Effective systems and clear evidence of quality.

items.name: Outstanding
items.desc: Strong systems and consistently high-quality practice. A model for the network.

blocks.title: There is no single school score
blocks.text: The five domains measure different things, and an average would hide the differences that matter for action. Eduversal **never publishes one composite score** for a school. A serious gap in one area cannot be balanced out by strength in another.
check: does not publish a single composite school score

blocks.title: Getting a visit right
do: Submit your Self-Evaluation **at least 5 working days** before each visit.
Keep evidence in the **Evidence Guide** workbook — it is the scoring document of record.
Use the visit day for discussion of your evidence, not for gathering it.
dont: Expecting a written report after Phase 1 — findings are shared in person.
Treating Specialist lesson observations as teacher scores — they are formative.
Comparing your ratings with other schools — ratings are against the standard.
check: Is there a written report after the first visit?

blocks.title: If you disagree with a rating

steps.title: Write to the CAO
steps.text: A formal written appeal within **10 working days** of receiving the report.

steps.title: Review
steps.text: The CAO reviews it with the relevant Domain Lead.

steps.title: Decision
steps.text: A response within **15 working days**. The CAO's decision is final.

check: within 10 working days of receiving the Annual School Quality Report

chapters.title: The Principal's leadership year
chapters.lede: An annual leadership review designed for growth and accountability — not a one-day inspection, and not the same as School Appraisal.

items.label: Developing level
items.note: Years in role are a guide; Eduversal confirms the level.

blocks.title: What makes up the Principal's score
blocks.intro: Leadership Observation is always the largest part. Outcomes count, but are capped at 15% because a principal does not control every factor.

items.name: F2 · Leadership Observation
items.desc: P1–P8 leadership areas, across two scheduled visits.

items.name: F1 · Operating Cadence
items.desc: How consistently the regular leadership rhythm is run and documented.

items.name: F3 · 360 Feedback

items.name: F5 · Self-Assessment
items.desc: Two termly self-assessments and an annual reflection.

do: Run the Principal Operating Cadence and keep evidence current.

blocks.title: Common questions

items.q: Does an Eduversal Specialist's observation change a teacher's score?
items.a: No. Specialist observations give the teacher Glow / Grow / Go feedback and help validate the school's Domain 2 picture. Only your school's own formal observations make up the F2 score.

items.q: What happens if a teacher has fewer than 3 formal observations in a semester?
items.a: F2 stays incomplete, and the final score should not be published until the requirement is met — or until school management agrees a documented exception in consultation with Eduversal.

items.q: Can a low observation be removed from the year's F2?
items.a: No. A high or low score, or the teacher disagreeing, is never a reason to remove a valid observation. Once it is valid and recorded, it stays in the calculation.

items.q: Do EASE or Cambridge results count in a teacher's appraisal?
items.a: No. EASE Growth, EASE Assessment and Cambridge results do not enter F1–F4 or level progression. They are read at school and network level in School Appraisal, never against an individual teacher.

items.q: Is there a written report after the first school visit?
items.a: No. Phase 1 findings are given in person and recorded in the Evidence Guide workbook. The one written report of the year comes after Phase 3.

items.q: Does the Impact Review in May–June change our ratings?
items.a: No. Phase 4 checks what changed for your two School Development Priorities. It creates no new Domain Rating and does not reopen the Phase 3 rating.

check: Once an observation is valid and recorded, it remains in the annual F2 calculation
